title: Twelve Weeks and One Empty Envelope
subtitle: 时间管理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 时间管理（生活与学习·时间管理与截止期限）
meta: 主题语境：时间管理（生活与学习·时间管理与截止期限）　|　核心词汇：deadline　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 deadline 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the editor ① set a deadline that no contributor in the office would have accepted, and he said the setting was the whole of the issue. The ② deadline, meaning the hour and not the limit, ran twelve weeks and stayed unmet on the board; a deadline, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left unwritten.

Every ③ deadline in that office had the same empty envelope beside it, and the ④ deadline at the end, meaning the one they kept for the last section and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever met twice. A deadline, his assistant said, is nine parts chasing and one part somebody willing to set; the editor said the chasing is the part that fills twelve weeks.

The printer meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the deadline was the whole of the schedule, meaning the limit and not the hour. The ⑥ deadline, meaning the limit and not any of that, is the only thing in a schedule that everybody agrees to and nobody reaches; deadline, he said, is either something you set or the only word that means both an hour and a limit. He said the limit is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ deadline had become a line in a contract, and the contract had become an argument about the empty envelope. The ⑧ deadline of the whole thing, the editor wrote in September, was one office and twelve weeks of chasing; deadline, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to chase. She said the chasing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ deadline I remember is the one at the end, which was met in 1986 and is still described as the strangest in the office. A ⑩ deadline, the assistant said in 1988, is the only thing that improves by being met; every deadline, she said, is a limit that has agreed to look like an hour. She said the limit was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 截止时间；最后期限（指办公室里定下的那一个）
B. n. 截止时间（指那个钟点本身，与那条界线相对）
C. 固定搭配：set a deadline 设定一个截止时间
D. n. 截止时间（指留给最后一个版面用的那一个）
E. n. 期限；截止（抽象总称，指一间办公室的全部催稿）
F. n. 期限（指合同里写到、被约定的那一条）
G. n. 期限；最后界线（指排期表上那条不可越过的线）
H. n. 界线（抽象总称，指人人答应却无人达到的那一条）

items.q: set a deadline that no contributor in the office would have accepted
The deadline, meaning the hour and not the limit
the deadline was the whole of the schedule
the deadline had become a line in a contract
The deadline of the whole thing

answers.why: set a deadline 意为“设定一个截止时间”，1967 年编辑定了一个办公室里没有一位撰稿人肯接受的截止时间。
deadline 意为“截止时间”，指那个钟点本身而不是那条界线，它在公告板上挂了十二个星期而没人赶上。
deadline 意为“截止时间”，指那间办公室里每一个截止时间，每一个旁边都有同一个空信封。
deadline 意为“截止时间”，指留给最后一个版面用的那一个，是唯一有人赶上过两次的。
deadline 意为“期限、最后界线”，指排期表上那条不可越过的线，印刷工说这条线就是那份排期的全部。
deadline 意为“界线”，指人人答应却无人达到的那一条而不是那个钟点，是排期里人人都答应、却无人赶到的东西。
deadline 意为“期限”，指合同里写到、被约定的那一条，到 1974 年这条期限成了合同里的一行。
deadline 意为“期限、截止”，编辑九月写道，整件事的截止是一间办公室和十二个星期的催稿。
deadline 意为“截止时间”，我记得的是末尾那一个，1986 年被赶上，至今仍被说成办公室里最奇的一次。
deadline 为抽象总称，助手 1988 年说，一个截止时间是唯一会因为被赶上而变得更好的东西。
